decisive_kills.reason: For the bounded cases that can be handled without tax judgment, the official rules reduce the core reconciliation to structured invoice/tax-document facts, actual production-use quantities and deterministic calculations. The official interpretation publishes worked formulas, so after ordinary data export the narrow ledger/output layer is reproducible with spreadsheet/agent tooling rather than requiring a distinct operator-controlled asset.

Current enterprise tax products already integrate business/production and finance data, invoice intake and deduction, automated tax calculation, declaration generation, policy-rule updates and audit trails. The proposed battery-specific reconciler sits inside an existing ERP/tax control surface that can absorb a new rule more naturally than a standalone entrant.

The only plausible differentiation is joining customer invoice/tax documents to ERP/MES production-consumption and product evidence. Those source systems and schemas vary by enterprise; without native system position, a third party risks recurring customer-specific implementation and mapping work.

Simple ledger/reconciliation cases are structured enough for incumbent tax software, spreadsheets or generic agents. Hard cases involve product-scope classification, mixed technologies, export allocation and other tax interpretation that the product must fail closed on and that professional tax advisers already address.

Search found broad paid enterprise tax software and professional tax advisory activity, but no current evidence that battery manufacturers pay separately for a standalone battery-consumption-tax reconciliation layer rather than using existing finance/ERP/tax staff and systems.

The governing rules are public and the decisive invoice, production-consumption, SKU and test-report data are customer-owned. The workflow does not naturally return a cross-customer outcome signal or execution right that compounds into a proprietary operator asset.

evidence.title: 财政部 海关总署 税务总局关于调整部分电池消费税政策的公告
evidence.fact: From 2026-09-01 specified batteries are taxed at 2%, rising to 4% from 2027-09-01; specified new-technology batteries receive temporary exemptions subject to standards.

evidence.title: 国家税务总局关于电池消费税征收管理有关事项的公告
evidence.fact: Taxpayers using tax-paid batteries to continue producing taxable batteries must establish the battery tax-credit ledger; exemption evidence must align test-report product lists with accounting and invoice names/specifications/models.

evidence.title: 关于《国家税务总局关于电池消费税征收管理有关事项的公告》的解读
evidence.fact: Worked examples calculate deductible tax from invoice/tax-payment amounts and actual production-use ratios, showing a deterministic structured core for uncomplicated cases.

evidence.title: 消费税政策即问即答之三
evidence.fact: Current official Q&A covers product-scope, mixed-cell, export and timing edge cases, showing that the difficult remainder is substantive tax classification and interpretation rather than mere ledger generation.

evidence.title: 金蝶EAS Cloud企业税务管理系统
evidence.fact: Current tax software integrates internal business/finance systems with tax systems and supports automated invoice intake, tax calculation, declaration, tax archives and risk management.

evidence.title: 财税管理系统2026选型：一体化管控财税，合规高效两不误
evidence.fact: Current manufacturing-focused tax/ERP tooling advertises production-finance linkage, invoice-to-production matching, automatic deduction handling and rapid adaptation to new tax policies.

evidence.title: 税务快讯｜德勤解读电池产品消费税新规：重塑产业格局
evidence.fact: Professional tax advisers already frame the new battery tax as a supply-chain, pricing, classification and compliance problem requiring enterprise impact analysis, evidencing an expert layer around the non-deterministic cases.
